title: Summarize `dgoss` test results for all images tested
description:
Running `dgoss` in `bakery` currently dumps all testing output sequentially into the output, including redirected output from `dgoss`. It also takes a fail-fast approach and will exit on the first error, which may be undesired behavior. We should find a way to take the results from `dgoss` and redirect them into a test summary file along with some human-readable output in the CLI.

## Goals
- [ ] Parse `dgoss` results output back into `bakery` for manipulation and summarizing.
- [ ] Provide a method for users to receive `dgoss` results summaries in the CLI output.
- [ ] Provide a method for users to receive all `dgoss` results formatted into one or more popular test result file formats (e.g. `junit`, `ctrf`, etc.).

## Notes
Consider reusing some ideas or code from the [pti blackbox runner](https://github.com/posit-dev/pti/blob/main/test/blackbox/blackbox_runner/report.py), which also utilizes `goss` results to create composite summaries in `ctrf`.

title: Revise tag override capabilities in `manifest.toml`
description:
Depends on #97 

We currently allow tags to be overridden in `manifest.toml` via `target.<name>.tags` or `target.<name>.latest`. These fields are then rendered via Jinja2 template. After discussions during work week, I can foresee this as being cumbersome.

Options to consider for making it more user friendly:
- Keep the same model, but add a reserved key word to add default tags into the mix. This could be as simple as doing `["{{ use_default }}", "extra_tag"]`. Assuming we run a `set` conversion on the tags, we shouldn't duplicate any on `bakery` operations.
- Refactor the tags as a TOML section with its own dictionary. This could be broken out by `all`, `default`, `latest`, and `primary_os` lists to define tags in those scenarios where `all` would apply to any set of `latest` and `primary_os` settings while `default` only applies to image variants without those flags.

title: [SPIKE] Investigate version granularity for directories and tags
description:
@bschwedler brought up the question of whether we want "full" versioned directories at the Work Week Docker session to the teams. Unfortunately, responses seemed largely mixed on whether to use full resolution versions (ex. `2024.11.0+467.pro1`) or any derivation down to the minor version only (ex. `2024.11`).

## Things to consider
- A standard should be applied to all products, otherwise we have to consider how to make `bakery` flexible to take what format of version a team wants to use.
- If patch iterations could break a user's environment, those versions need to have a distinct tag and possibly should maintain their rebuild-ability.
- What are customers feelings towards patch versions? I have a feeling they would not want to be forcibly upgraded in many situations and most of our customers, particularly smaller to medium sized ones, do not have very actively monitored and managed environments. Customers may not understand how to pin to something like a specific tag or SHA in all cases.

## What this decision may affect
- How do we best track versioned directories? Previously, we had appended a version to the parent directory of the `manifest.toml` to resolve resources like Containerfiles. How do we resolve those directories if the full version does not necessarily match up between what the directory's name is and what the version listed in `manifest.toml` is?
- How do versions get written into associated template renderings? Do users always pass the "full" version and either by standard or configuration setting `bakery` knows what version to place as the directory name?

title: [SPIKE] Evaluate how to implement a "primary OS" concept
description:
We need to look into the "primary OS" setting again because someone brought up a good point about customers potentially pulling a `:latest` or `:<version>` tag and having it potentially switch up their OS down the line.

---

I propose having "primary OS" as a per build field in `manifest.toml`, for example:
```toml
[build."2024.11.0"]
latest = true
os = ["Ubuntu 22.04", "Ubuntu 24.04"]
primary_os = "Ubuntu 22.04"
```

This would then tell `bakery` to only utilize `latest` type tags and the raw `<version>` tag on that OS's image builds. Since this extra setting does go against our desire for "mostly defaults", we should consider how to handle any situations where the `primary_os` key is not present. I think there are three obvious options:
1. Require the field. I don't like this one.
2. If `primary_os` is not present, set it to the first defined OS in the build's `os` list.
3. If `primary_os` is not present, forgo producing any more general tags that exclude the OS for the image build (`latest` and `<version>` will not be available, only `<os>`, `<version>-<os>`, etc.).

title: Default image tags do not render as originally specced
description:
Image tags are rendering outside of the original ruleset we made. This is a regression moving from the previous implementation to using the much cleaner Pydantic models system.

## Tasks
- [ ] Fix tag logic based on decided tag formatting.
- [ ] Document tag logic for `bakery` end users.
- [ ] Ensure permutations of tag logic are well-covered by tests.

## Behavior
### Expected
#### std
- Default
  - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:<version>-<os>`
  - For Primary OS
    - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:<version>`
- Latest
  - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:latest-<os>`
  - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:<os>`
  - For Primary OS
    - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:latest`

#### min (and other types)
- Default
  - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:<version>-<os>-<type>`
  - For Primary OS
    - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:<version>-<type>`
- Latest
  - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:latest-<os>-<type>`
  - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:<os>-<type>`
  - For Primary OS
    - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:latest-<type>`
    - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:<type>`

### Actual
#### all types (std and min)
- Default
  - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:<version>-<os>`
- Latest
  - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:<os>-<type>`
  - `<host>/<namespace>/<image_name>:latest` 
    - **This is a big issue because it duplicates a tag across multiple images.**

## Notes
- We do not currently have a concept of "Primary OS". See #98.
- `std` should be considered the "default" type and should not append its type.

title: `BuildOS` unnecessarily overrides `__init__` method

Since the `__init__` only extrapolates the `pretty` and `condensed` fields, I think it would be easier for us to define them as `computed_field`s.

title: Fix `bakery render` command after TOML object refactor
description:
Various errors occur when rendering new or over existing versions of an image after merging #86.

Issues identified:
- Rendering over existing versions throws an error instead of re-rendering the version.
  - Expected: Render overwrites existing image files with new image files from rendered templates. Build manifest is either unchanged or rewritten as if it's a new version.
  - Actual: A `BakeryConfigError` exception is raised.
- Template values are not passed to `jinja2` templates.
  - Expected: Values passed in using `--value` are given to the Jinja2 template engine to render templates.
  - Actual: Values are parsed in the CLI, but not passed down to template rendering.
- Rendering a version fails for new `manifest.toml` files created by `bakery new`.
  - Expected: A new `[build.<VERSION>]` section is added for the new version passed to `bakery render`.
  - Actual: `Manifest.add_version` expects `build` to already exist as a section and produces a `KeyError` rather than creating a new empty dictionary for the `build` section.

description:

title: Implement `openscap` tool in `bakery` for image hardening
description:
Rather than pursuing hardened images by using a hardened base image (e.g. wolfi or distroless), we can opt to harden our images based on CIS Benchmarks for server hardening. The OpenSCAP tool is provided as an [image by Chainguard](https://images.chainguard.dev/directory/image/openscap/overview) and can allow us to test our images against policies provided by the Security Team and remediate violations.

@aja08379 has created a Github Action to scan an image in a repository against the desired policy standard. Reviewing the Github Action will be immensely helpful for understanding how best to implement OpenSCAP and could possibly be used long-term in Workbench for Snowflake as long as they maintain their own image.

OpenSCAP seems like another tool we could easily implement as another extension to `bakery` like `dgoss` and `snyk`. Ideally, we will want a way to consume standard runtime options and policy standards upstream from the Security team rather than updating individual repositories over time.

Currently, only Ubuntu 22.04 is supported for benchmarking so any hardened images we provide must be based on that version. The Security Team suggests only maintaining _one_ version of the hardened image, but I could foresee "hardened" becoming another image type in the future alongside "min" and "std". To our knowledge, the only product with hardened demand is Workbench.

We should implement formatting via `go fmt`, or preferably via the stricter [gofumpt](https://github.com/mvdan/gofumpt) and [golines](https://github.com/segmentio/golines). These tools should be enforced via CI and pre-commit and be available in `just`. We should also consider a linter like [golangci-lint](https://golangci-lint.run/usage/linters/) to ensure we follow best practices.

Since Go is already fairly strict and uniform about formatting via `go fmt` (which is what my IDE implements), I don't expect a ton of direct code changes.

title: Move posit-bakery into src/ directory
Improve `rich` usage and unify logging/printing
description:
Our usage of `rich` (package we use to make `print` fancy) is all over the place. I think it would be helpful to consider unifying and how we use `rich` across `bakery`. Some possible areas to investigate:

- `rich` has a drop in enhancement/replacement for logging. Should some/most/all of our current `print` statements be logs instead?
- How surface level should `print` statements be? Should stuff within classes be using logging instead?
- Can we create some common patterns or functions for stylizing different messages? For example, can we more easily stylize Warnings and Errors so we don't have to repeatedly use `rich`'s error-prone markup inside a string?
- Can we implement some testing around expected logging/print outputs where it may be key for a user to get those messages?
- Can we implement quiet/debug type flags in our CLI?

title: Enforce TOML document schema using pydantic
description:
Right now, TOML structure for Manifests and Configs is only loosely enforced. This is because we need to have a class that helps us extrapolate, manipulate, and manage the underlying data of the Manifest and Config TOML documents. This can cause problems as we go to ingest or modify elements of the TOML document that are missing or are not laid out as we expect. 

To fix this problem we could add an intermediary pydantic model that directly represents the data in a Config or Manifest. By directly representing the fields that we expect to be present, we can enhance our file validation and isolation of errors. This model would also better preserve the document state. This model could then be ingested or used by another class that represents our additional functionality on top of this data.

Essentially we would go from
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    config.toml --> Config
    Config --> Manifest
    manifest.toml --> Manifest
```
to
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    config.toml --> ConfigToml
    manifest.toml --> ManifestToml
    ConfigToml --> Config
    ManifestToml --> Manifest
    Config --> Manifest
```

description:
## Background
The rstudio/rstudio-docker-products repo has a long history with both our internal staff and external users. While there are good elements of it that we would like to keep, such as:
- Abstraction of product complexity
- Parallel, structured image builds
- Consistent linting, validation, and vulnerability scans
- Mostly positive general operation

There are also many elements that make the repo a negative experience for both internal and external users such as:
- Large, overengineered images
- Large, overcomplicated tags
- Incomplete labeling
- Complex overly integrated build/test workflows
- Inconsistent vulnerability patches for in support product versions
- Overabundance of bridging Justfile commands
- Licensing operation inconsistencies
- Confusing, repetitive configurations
- Confusion over shared ownership of repo

## Goals 
In an attempt to resolve a majority of these issues, I want to prototype a large scale rewrite of the repository and propose it to the Platform and Product teams as a new way forward. In this prototype, I want to directly address:
- Division of responsibilities and ownership
  - Migrate from single repo to definitively owned individual repos for each component image
  - Move Platform's role from image ownership to common fabric/tools ownership
  - Give team's full responsibility and governance over their images with Platform in an advisory capacity
- Overly integrated and complex workflows
  - Dividing up repositories will sever build interdependence of unrelated product team builds
  - We can still share workflow code via Platform team shared code
- Image size
  - Remove Python/R version duplication and strip out as many unrelated libraries as possible for product images
  - Provide a "minimal" image that does not include dependencies such as Python and R out of the box
- Overuse of Just commands
  - Move logic in Just code to maintainable and testable CLI tool for negotiating configurations with varying tools such as Bake, Goss, Snyk, etc.
- Confusing, repetitive configurations
  - Use explicit versions in image definitions
  - Create a template configuration that can be used for all images

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Prototype a common tool that removes complexity around configuration and tool integration
- [ ] Prototype a common configuration format that reduces configuration repetition across projects
- [ ] Prototype a slimmed down base image that includes only the Ubuntu base OS and helper scripts for use downstream
- [ ] Prototype each product image in the new standard/minimal formats
- [ ] Document extending of images downstream
- [ ] Get buy-in from product teams on new prototype

## Issues In This Epic

### Issues

title: Fix yq -i reformatting that breaks helm chart lint
description:
The `product-release.yml` workflow in `rstudio/helm` uses `yq -i` to
update `values.yaml` in place, which re-serializes the whole file and
drops formatting that `ct lint` requires. This broke the auto-generated
release PR's lint check.

rstudio/helm PR #917 (dispatched from this repo's images-connect
production release) failed with:

    479:27 [comments] too few spaces before comment
    480:28 [comments] too few spaces before comment
    482:29 [comments] too few spaces before comment

The diff shows why: yq's re-serialization collapsed inline comment
padding from 2 spaces to 1 (e.g. `ServiceLogLevel: INFO  # ...` became
`ServiceLogLevel: INFO # ...`) and stripped ~75 blank lines that
separated top-level and nested keys throughout the file. `ct lint`'s
embedded yamllint config requires `min-spaces-from-content: 2`, so any
comment yq collapses to 1 space fails the job.

The "Sync Connect interpreter paths" step is the culprit — it's the
only step that rewrites `values.yaml` as a whole document (the
Chart.yaml bump step only touches `Chart.yaml`):

    yq -i ".config.Python.Executable = [...]" "charts/${CHART_NAME}/values.yaml"

Possible directions:
- Replace the `yq -i` on `values.yaml` with a targeted substitution
  (e.g. `sed`) that touches only the one field, avoiding a
  full-document re-serialization.
- Add a normalization step after any `yq -i` call that restores
  minimum-2-space comment padding before the PR is opened.

- https://github.com/rstudio/helm/pull/917

title: Eliminate error messages from missing cache artifacts on first run
description:
On the first run of a workflow (or when the artifact cache is missing), the `Restore dependency version cache` step in `setup-bakery` attempts to download a non-existent artifact, producing error messages like:
```
Unable to download artifact(s): Artifact not found for name: bakery-deps-*
Please ensure that your artifact is not expired and the artifact ...
```

Although the workflow continues due to `continue-on-error: true`, these error messages appear as failed steps in job logs, creating noise and confusion.

## Expected behavior

The cache restore should fail gracefully on first run without producing visible error messages, while still showing actual retrieval failures (permissions, expiration, network issues).

## Possible approach

Query the GitHub API in a bash step to check if the expected cache artifact exists before attempting to download it, conditionally running the `download-artifact` action only when the artifact exists.

## Files affected

- `setup-bakery/action.yml`

title: Spike: determine signing/attestation method for container images
description:
Part of #453.

Determine which mechanism Posit should use to produce and sign build-provenance/SBOM attestations for published container images, before the implementation sub-issues below are scoped precisely.

Candidates to evaluate: GitHub Artifact Attestations (Sigstore-backed), Notation/Notary v2, self-managed cosign + KMS, others surfaced during investigation.

Deliverable: a documented recommendation (method + rationale) that the implementation sub-issues can be scoped against.

Starting point / research so far:

| Option | Trust model | Key mgmt | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GitHub Artifact Attestations | Sigstore (Fulcio/Rekor), keyless OIDC | None | Verifiable via `gh attestation verify` or `cosign verify-attestation` (>=2.4.0). The SLSA project itself is deprecating its standalone `slsa-github-generator` in favor of this. |
| Notation / Notary v2 | Hierarchical PKI, TUF | Certs/HSM | Supports multiple independent signatures per image (e.g. build + separate compliance sign-off). Recommended more for enterprises with existing PKI than OSS projects. |
| Self-managed cosign + KMS | Sigstore tooling, static keys | KMS-backed keypair | Avoids depending on public Fulcio/Rekor; loses keyless convenience and public transparency log unless Rekor is self-hosted too. |
| Docker Content Trust (Notary v1) | Hierarchical, offline keys | Notary server + MySQL + mTLS | Legacy; one signature per image max, no multi-registry portability. |
| GPG/PGP | Web of trust | Manual | No OCI-native signature distribution; industry is actively moving away from it. |

Given our images are public, multi-registry (Docker Hub + GHCR + ECR), and built exclusively on GitHub Actions, GitHub Artifact Attestations is the leading candidate — but this issue should produce a documented decision rather than assume it.

title: gcc-toolset install macro for Rocky/RHEL-family images
description:
## Problem

Posit's own product images (package-manager/connect/workbench) never compile anything — R, Python, and the products themselves install as prebuilt binaries/RPMs, so bakery has no toolchain-installation macro today. Self-service customers installing arbitrary R/Python packages (e.g., once `pak::pkg_sysreqs` resolution lands) may need to compile native dependencies from source, especially on older RHEL-family bases lacking newer prebuilt libraries.

container-generator conditionally installs `gcc-toolset-{9..14}` on Rocky/RHEL and sources it via `/etc/bashrc`.

## Scope

A macro parallel to dnf.j2 for enabling a given `gcc-toolset-N` on Rocky/RHEL/Alma, including the `/etc/bashrc` sourcing step.

title: RHEL subscription-manager macro or documented pattern for self-service images
description:
## Problem

Self-service customers building their own images (unlike Posit's own first-party product images, which only ever target UBI — see images-shared#575) may target full subscription-gated RHEL rather than UBI. Bakery has no pattern for this today: `BuildSecret` (`config/image/build_secret.py`) is a generic mechanism for passing secrets to `docker buildx build`, but nothing wires it to `subscription-manager register` or conditional CodeReady Builder enablement.

container-generator's own approach: Red Hat credentials in a separate `.pw` file, copied in and deleted after registration, with conditional CRB/EPEL enablement differing between RHEL 8 and 9.

## Scope

A macro (or documented pattern, if a macro is overkill for what's essentially one `subscription-manager register` call plus cleanup) parallel to the existing package-manager macros (apt.j2/dnf.j2), using `BuildSecret` for credential passing rather than embedding credentials in the Containerfile.

## Non-goal

Distinct from images-shared#575's UBI work — UBI is deliberately subscription-free, so this pattern is never needed there.

title: Add `bakery create image --interactive` wizard with template assembly
description:
## Problem

`bakery create image` scaffolds a *commented-out* stub Containerfile.jinja2 (`posit_bakery/config/templating/templates/Containerfile.jinja2`) — real macro imports are pre-written, but every section is just a comment telling a human what to fill in. Nothing about OS family, R/Python/Quarto versions, or system packages flows into it; a user has to already know bakery's macro vocabulary (apt.j2/dnf.j2/python.j2/r.j2/quarto.j2/goss.j2) to produce a working Containerfile.

This is the residual gap identified from analyzing michaelmayer2/container-generator: its UI walks a customer through exactly these choices and writes a working Dockerfile. This issue is bakery's answer, as an opt-in CLI wizard rather than a second tool to maintain.

## Design

**Flag:** `-i, --interactive` on the existing `bakery create image` command, opt-in (tool remains non-interactive by default, consistent with `create version`/`create matrix`/`create project`, all used from CI). Any flag given explicitly on the command line is never re-prompted.

**Prompt sequence:**
1. Image name (skipped if given positionally)
2. OS family + version, sourced from `SUPPORTED_OS` (`build_os.py`), defaulting to bakery's existing `DEFAULT_OS`
3. Languages to include (multi-select: R, Python, Quarto, or none)
4. Per selected language: version(s) — space-separated, or `latest` (resolved via the same `DependencyConstraint`/"latest" machinery `create matrix --dependency-constraint` already uses)
5. Extra system packages (optional free text → `deps/packages.txt`)
6. Generate goss tests for these installs? [Y/n]
7. If any language got multiple versions: create a matrix instead of one version? [Y/n]
8. Version name (or matrix name-pattern)
9. **Confirmation gate**: a summary of every file to be created/changed (reusing the existing `dirdiff`/`render_markdown` helpers `create_version --diff-against` already uses). Nothing is written until explicit confirmation — a Ctrl-C or "no" leaves zero side effects, since all writes happen in one place at the end.

**Architecture** (three new pieces, nothing existing modified):

- `posit_bakery/cli/interactive.py` — prompt flow + confirmation gate; builds a `WizardAnswers` object, then calls the existing, unmodified `BakeryConfig.create_image()`/`create_version()`/`create_matrix()`.
- `posit_bakery/config/templating/interactive_assembly.py` — pure functions (`assemble_containerfile`, `assemble_deps_file`, `assemble_goss_file`), no I/O, no prompting. Loads and concatenates fragment files into the same section-header shape the current stub already has.
- `posit_bakery/config/templating/templates/interactive_fragments/` — small `.jinja2` fragments, one per concern (`apt_setup.jinja2`, `dnf_setup.jinja2`, `r_install.jinja2`, `python_install.jinja2`, `quarto_install.jinja2`, `goss/{r,python,quarto}.jinja2`), each just the macro call a human would write by hand.

Chosen over curated per-combination presets (combinatorial — 2 package managers × 8 language combinations — and drifts from real macros over time, the exact problem with container-generator's own hardcoded duplicate of bakery's OS/version logic) and over Python-side string-built Jinja2 (fragile, hard to unit-test in isolation). Adding a language later means adding one fragment file, not touching assembly logic.

**Error handling:**

- Version input validated via the existing `RDependencyVersions`/`PythonDependencyVersions`/`QuartoDependencyVersions` pydantic models, catching `ValidationError` for a re-prompt.
- Network failure fetching available versions surfaces the same as everywhere else in bakery today (hard error) — no new silent-degradation path specific to this command.
- Image name collision checked immediately after the name is entered, not after the full wizard.
- Version/matrix render failures reuse `create_version`/`create_matrix`'s existing cleanup (already removes a partially-created version directory on `BakeryRenderError`).

**Testing:** assembler as pure input→string tests; full wizard flow via typer's `CliRunner` with scripted stdin; explicit test that declining confirmation leaves the filesystem and `bakery.yaml` untouched; bad-version retry behavior.

title: 🏗️ Self-service execution-environment image creation
description:
## Background

container-generator is a self-service Shiny app that generates Dockerfiles/Singularity definitions plus Posit Connect off-host `values.yaml`, letting a customer pick an OS, R/Python/Quarto versions, and Pro Drivers and download a working build. It's a demand signal for a bakery-native answer — this epic is that answer, scoped to bakery + images-examples rather than a second tool to maintain.

## Definition of done

A customer with no bakery experience can go from "I need R 4.4.2 + Python 3.12 + Quarto on Rocky 9" to a tested, buildable Containerfile — and, once the dependent work below lands, a generated Connect off-host `values.yaml` — using bakery and images-examples alone.

## Depends on (not filed here — not yet real issues anywhere)

- Project-level artifact templates rendered over an image's version matrix, to generate Connect `values.yaml`. Blocking: `Image.template_path` (`posit_bakery/config/image/image.py:299`) and the render loop (`matrix.py:538-543`) scope template rendering to one image at a time; there's no aggregation point across images yet.
- Automatic R system-dependency resolution via `pak::pkg_sysreqs`, replacing hand-maintained `deps/system-packages.txt`.

Both were identified as prerequisites while scoping this epic but were never filed as standalone issues anywhere — worth doing before or alongside the sub-issues below.

## Checklist (break out into issues when picked up)

- Pro Drivers on a bare-OS base, not just atop Posit's own `-min` images — could fold into the worked-example sub-issue rather than a standalone macro.
- Apptainer/Singularity output — open question, not yet decided. The Posit Team image fleet management epic scoped this down to a consumption doc only (convert bakery-built OCI images via `apptainer build`); this epic's actual premise (hand the customer whatever artifact they asked for) is what reopens it.

## Non-goals

- GUI front end — resolved in favor of `bakery create image --interactive` instead.
- "Install every package from a repo" mode.
- Full package-level/environment locks

title: RHEL 10 falls through to `multi` in `_parse_download_json_os_identifier` for Connect and Package Manager
description:
## Problem

`_parse_download_json_os_identifier` (`posit_bakery/config/image/posit_product/main.py`) hardcodes RHEL-family version handling per product and silently falls through to a `"multi"` OS identifier for RHEL 10 in two of three branches:

- `ProductEnum.CONNECT`: handles versions 8 (`redhat8`) and 9 (`rhel9`); nothing for 10.
- `ProductEnum.PACKAGE_MANAGER`: handles versions 7 (`rhel7_64`), 8 (`fedora28`), 9 (`rhel9`); nothing for 10.
- `ProductEnum.WORKBENCH`/`WORKBENCH_SESSION`: already generic (`"rhel" + _os.version`), unaffected.

The fallthrough means the release-channel resolver silently looks up the wrong `download_json_os` key when fetching version/download-URL metadata for a RHEL 10 build, instead of failing loudly.

## Where

- `posit_bakery/config/image/posit_product/main.py:296-334` (`_parse_download_json_os_identifier`)

## Why fix it here, not in each product repo

images-package-manager#130 already plans to patch the `PACKAGE_MANAGER` branch as part of its own RHEL 10 (UBI) work. This file is shared library code in images-shared (posit-bakery), consumed by every product repo — patching only the `PACKAGE_MANAGER` branch there doesn't help images-connect#143, which will independently hit the identical fallthrough for the `CONNECT` branch and need the same file patched again, plus a new posit-bakery release either way. Fixing both branches together here avoids that duplication.

## Note

Package Manager's own version-to-identifier mapping isn't a clean function of version number (`rhel7_64`, `fedora28`, `rhel9`), so this likely isn't a one-line `elif`. Confirm what identifier Connect's and Package Manager's `downloads.json` actually publish for RHEL 10 once artifacts exist there, for both branches, before wiring in a value.

## Related

- https://github.com/posit-dev/images-shared/issues/575
- https://github.com/posit-dev/images-package-manager/issues/130
- https://github.com/posit-dev/images-connect/issues/143
- https://github.com/posit-dev/images-shared/issues/666

title: Design: model UBI as a first-class concept in the bakery OS schema
description:
Follow-up from posit-dev/images-shared#575 (RHEL 10 (UBI) image
support).

The bakery OS schema (`OSFamilyEnum`, `SUPPORTED_OS` in
`posit_bakery/config/image/build_os.py`) already models RHEL versions
8/9/10 and sibling distros (Alma, Rocky). It has no concept of "UBI"
anywhere — posit-dev/images-package-manager#130 works around this by
hardcoding `registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/ubi` directly in the
Containerfile template rather than expressing it in `bakery.yaml`.

## Question

Is RHEL-family + version sufficient, with "which base image the
Containerfile pulls from" left as an implementation detail (the current
pattern) — or should UBI be a first-class schema concept (e.g. a
`baseImage` field) before three product repos independently hardcode it?

## Notes

Not blocking Phase 1-3 work — package-manager, connect, and workbench
can all follow the existing hardcoded pattern in the meantime.

title: Add `bakery build --summary` for build/tag/size counts
description:
`bakery build` fans out into dozens of image builds and hundreds of pushed tags per product repo, but nothing reports the shape or cost of that work. Today the only way to find out is hand-counting `--plan` JSON output. Measured live across the three product repos:

| Repo | Bake targets | Registry tags | Platform builds |
|---|---|---|---|
| images-connect | 53 | 272 | 64 |
| images-workbench | 30 | 286 | 39 |
| images-package-manager | 24 | 180 | 32 |

Add a `--summary` flag to report counts (and, eventually, image/cache sizes) for whatever the current filters selected, as a human-readable table or JSON for CI.

This ships in phases:

- [ ] **Phase 1 (counts, no I/O)** — build target, platform build, and registry tag counts, derived from already-resolved config so every existing filter flag works for free.
- [ ] **Phase 2 (image sizes)** — registry (compressed) and local (uncompressed) size columns, populated after a real build via `python_on_whales`.
- [ ] **Phase 3 (cache size)** — layer cache size per target, needs a new read-only GHCR registry v2 client (`ghcr.io`), since the registry Packages API (`api.github.com`) bakery currently talks to exposes no size field at all.

title: Add oven: a local build, test, validate, and scan environment
description:
A contributor cannot build, test, validate, and scan a product image on a local computer today. Each task needs its own tool, and each tool exists only as a step inside GitHub Actions:

- goss and dgoss
- hadolint
- wizcli
- trivy
- oras
- Docker Buildx

There is no single, repeatable way to install all of these tools on one computer.

The proposed container holds all of these tools. Its name is "the oven".

The oven uses Docker-outside-of-Docker. With this method, the oven sends commands to the host's own Docker daemon. The oven does not run a second daemon inside itself.

A `just oven` command builds the oven if it is not current, then starts it. This command mounts each sibling product repository at the same path inside the oven and on the host. As a result, `bakery build` and `dgoss run` work the same way inside the oven as they do on the host.

title: Parallel build logs have doubled newlines and blank separator lines
description:
`bakery build --strategy build` streams buildx output through `PrefixedLogSink.write()`, prefixed per target. Two bugs make it hard to read:

- buildx's blank step-separator lines print as a bare `[key]` with no content.

title: Packaging 26.2 breaks DependencyVersion deepcopy and dependency resolution
description:
## Summary

`just posit-bakery/test` fails broadly after upgrading `packaging` from 25.0 to 26.2. The failures all originate from `DependencyVersion` losing its subclass attributes during `copy.deepcopy()`.

## Reproduction

On commit `3e0391c0`:

```text
cd posit-bakery
just test
```

Result: 71 failed, 1984 passed.

A minimal reproduction is:

```python
import copy
from posit_bakery.config.dependencies.version import DependencyVersion

version = copy.deepcopy(DependencyVersion("3.13.7"))
print(version.minor)
```

With `packaging==26.2`, this raises:

```text
AttributeError: 'DependencyVersion' object has no attribute '_has_minor'
```

The same reproduction works with `packaging==25.0`.

## Cause

`DependencyVersion` subclasses `packaging.version.Version` and adds `_has_minor`, `_has_micro`, and `_original`. The dependency providers intentionally deep-copy cached versions in:

- `posit_bakery/config/dependencies/python.py`
- `posit_bakery/config/dependencies/r.py`
- `posit_bakery/config/dependencies/quarto.py`
- `posit_bakery/config/dependencies/positron.py`

Packaging 26.2 changed `Version` to a slotted/stable-pickle implementation. Its copy/deepcopy state does not preserve these subclass attributes, so dependency resolution fails when accessing `v.minor`.

The triggering change in this branch is the dependency update in commit `3e0391c0`, which changed:

```diff
- packaging>=25.0,<26.0
+ packaging>=25.0,<27.0
```

and locked `packaging` to 26.2.

## Expected behavior

Dependency versions should remain usable after the documented defensive deep-copy operation, and the test suite should pass with the supported packaging range.

## Possible fixes

Either restore the `<26.0` upper bound temporarily, or update `DependencyVersion`/the caching strategy so its subclass state survives copying while retaining compatibility with packaging 26.x.

title: setup-hadolint/setup-goss: checksum and URL bugs for pinned versions
description:
setup-hadolint and setup-goss each have a dormant bug. A review of oven/Containerfile on branch feat/bakery-oven found both.

**setup-hadolint**: GitHub matches download URLs without case. So the fallback from `hadolint-linux-${arch}` to `hadolint-Linux-${arch}` never runs, because the lowercase request always succeeds. For hadolint versions before v2.13.0, the script saves the binary under the wrong filename. Then the checksum check fails.

**setup-goss**: the "Install dgoss" step builds the URL as `releases/${version}/download/dgoss`. GitHub's real pattern is `releases/download/${tag}/dgoss`. The old URL works only when `version` is `"latest"`. Any pinned version returns a 404 error.

Both bugs are dormant now. Every caller uses the default value `"latest"` for both actions. If anyone pins an older version, the bugs will occur.

title: Upload bakery trivy scan SARIF results to GitHub code scanning
description:
bakery trivy scan (#218, #722) now writes SARIF per target to results/trivy/, but doesn't upload it to GitHub code scanning. - [ ] Add security-events: write to each of images-connect/images-workbench/images-package-manager's calling jobs
- [ ] Re-add security-events: write and the github/codeql-action/upload-sarif step to bakery-build-native.yml's build-test job
- [ ] Sequence: merge the three product-repo permission grants before merging the images-shared re-add, so no caller is ever left mid-transition without a permission its currently-running workflow file expects

title: Spike: investigate bake build metadata for native workflow migration
description:
## Context

`.github/workflows/bakery-build-native.yml` currently invokes `bakery build --strategy build` once per image/platform and writes one metadata JSON artifact per build. The merge job downloads those files and passes them to `bakery ci publish`.

Bakery supports `--strategy bake`, which may simplify or improve the native build workflow, but the metadata emitted by a bake build may differ from the metadata currently consumed by the test and publish stages.

## Spike

Investigate the metadata output from `bakery build --strategy bake` and determine whether the native workflow can migrate from `--strategy build` without losing or changing required image information.

Compare `build` and `bake` outputs for representative single-platform and multi-target builds, including:

- metadata file shape and target/UID mapping;
- image name/tag and digest values;
- platform detection and per-platform metadata;
- OCI descriptor and creation annotations;
- build provenance fields;
- behavior with `--push`, temporary registries, cache settings, and retries;
- compatibility with `bakery dgoss run` and `bakery ci publish`;
- artifact naming/aggregation in the `build-test` and `merge` jobs.

Use a disposable or manually dispatched workflow run where practical. Do not change the production strategy as part of this spike.

## Deliverables

- Documented comparison of representative `build` and `bake` metadata files.
- Identified gaps, incompatibilities, or required Bakery changes/tests.
- Recommendation on whether to migrate, including a high-level follow-up implementation plan if migration is viable.
- If viable, a proposed workflow diff or follow-up issue covering the required changes to `.github/workflows/bakery-build-native.yml`.

## Acceptance criteria

- The metadata contract required by `bakery dgoss run` and `bakery ci publish` is explicitly documented.
- The recommendation is backed by actual build outputs and validation of both consumers.
- Any changes needed in Bakery or the workflow are captured as actionable follow-up work.
